prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals in the Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 (ideology-free)

- Economy and tax: Invest in renewables, home insulation and green infrastructure; repair EU trade ties; responsible public finances; priority future tax cut via higher personal allowance; reverse bank tax cuts; one-off proper windfall tax on oil/gas; raise Digital Services Tax to 6%; fairer capital gains tax; 4% levy on FTSE-100 buybacks; expand British Business Bank; national financial inclusion strategy.

- Business, jobs and work: Statutory Industrial Strategy and Council; 3–3.5% of GDP on R&D; Horizon Europe/EIC participation; AI cross-sector regulation; Parliament to approve trade mandates/deals; abolish business rates, replace with a Commercial Landowner Levy; local banking; prompt payment enforcement. Skills: replace apprenticeship levy with flexible skills levy; National Colleges; Lifelong Skills Grants (£5,000, aiming £10,000). Work rights: new “dependent contractor” status; zero-hours protections; living wage review; fix Statutory Sick Pay; Worker Protection Enforcement Authority.

- Climate and energy: Net zero by 2045; 90% electricity from renewables by 2030; 10‑year home upgrade (free insulation/heat pumps for low-income); zero‑carbon new builds; rooftop solar incentives; social energy tariff; decouple electricity from gas prices; remove barriers to wind/solar; ban fracking/new coal; end fossil subsidies with just transition; invest in storage and interconnectors; scale community energy; carbon border adjustment; greener public procurement.

- Health and social care: Right to see GP within 7 days/24h urgent (8,000 more GPs); urgent NHS dentistry access; mental health hubs in every community, school MH professionals, regular check‑ups; 62‑day cancer treatment guarantee; pharmacy first; 10‑year hospital estate plan; digital interoperability; EMA mutual recognition for faster medicines; drugs policy focused on health and regulated cannabis market. Care: free personal care; workforce plan, Royal College, Carer’s Minimum Wage (+£2/h); unpaid carers’ paid leave and respite; National Care Agency; transferable care packages.

- Education and families: Per‑pupil funding above inflation; building repairs; Tutoring Guarantee; early‑years boost (extra hours; triple Early Years Pupil Premium); maintenance grants restored; teacher workforce strategy and independent pay body; SEND funding/national body; Ofsted reform; arts in EBacc; Young People’s Premium (16–18); Erasmus+ return. Families: free school meals for all children in poverty (aim all primary); day‑one parental rights incl. self‑employed; double maternity/shared pay to £350; paternity at 90% pay plus extra month; paid neonatal leave; childcare funding rates review; childminding reform.

- Welfare and pensions: Scrap two‑child limit and benefit cap; UC first payment in 5 days; end sanctions regime; protect triple lock; WASPI compensation; increase and widen Carer’s Allowance; disability benefit assessment reforms; address gender pension gap.

- Crime and justice: Restore community policing; guarantee police attendance/investigation of all burglaries; Online Crime Agency; scrap Police & Crime Commissioners (local Police Boards instead); halve offence‑to‑sentence time; expand youth diversion; strengthen response to VAWG; justice system workforce/data strategies; modern slavery protections; prison rehabilitation, women’s justice board.

- Environment and farming: Transform water companies to public benefit companies; ban bonuses until discharges/leaks end; new tough regulator; Sewage Tax; binding 2030 targets for bathing/sensitive sites; Clean Air Act (WHO limits) with new agency; “double nature” by 2050; 60m trees/year; 30% land/sea protected by 2030; deposit return scheme; eliminate non‑recyclable single‑use plastics in 3 years; peatland restoration. Food/farming: National Food Strategy; +£1bn/year to Environmental Land Management; veterinary/plant‑health deals with EU; strengthen Groceries Code Adjudicator; high welfare/trade standards; fisheries sustainability.

- Housing and local government: 380,000 homes/year incl. 150,000 social; 10 garden cities; abolish leasehold and cap ground rents; end Section 21, default 3‑year tenancies, landlord register; allow councils to end Right to Buy; rough sleeping ended next Parliament; councils buy land at use value; plan‑dept funding; brownfield with affordable; “use‑it‑or‑lose‑it” permissions; zero‑carbon new homes; cladding removed at no cost to leaseholders; Rent‑to‑Own for social housing. Local powers over second homes/short lets; gigabit broadband nationwide.

- Transport: Rapid EV charging rollout; restore plug‑in grant; 2030 zero‑emission sales; cut VAT on public charging to 5%; freeze rail fares; Railway Agency; sanction failing operators; major rail electrification, Northern Powerhouse Rail; bus franchising powers and funding reform; £2 fare cap while reviewed; active travel networks; shift more roads budget to maintenance; private jet super tax; restrict short flights where <2.5h rail exists.

- Culture and media: Protect BBC/S4C/Channel 4; Creative Europe; EU touring facilitation; Anti‑SLAPP law; on‑demand accessibility quotas; football regulator; gambling levy, ad restrictions, Ombudsman.

- Immigration and asylum: End Hostile Environment; move work/ student visa policy out of Home Office; scrap Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda plan; 3‑month asylum decision standard; right to work after 3 months; expand safe/legal routes; flexible, sector‑based work visa system; reverse family visa threshold rise; Settled Status protections; Windrush redress; firewall between services and enforcement.

- Rights and political reform: Uphold Human Rights Act/ECHR; ban conversion practices; Digital Bill of Rights; regulate biometrics; votes at 16; PR by STV for MPs and English councils; cap donations; codify Ministerial Code; House of Lords reform; federal UK with stronger devolution; transparency on lobbying/messaging.

- Defence and international: Increase defence spending towards 2.5% GDP; reverse Army cuts; maintain nuclear deterrent; tighter arms export controls; parliamentary vote before action; deepen European security cooperation; support Ukraine (incl. seizing Russian assets for aid); restore 0.7% aid with independent department; Gaza–Israel immediate bilateral ceasefire, recognise Palestine, two‑state solution; strengthen sanctions and anti‑kleptocracy measures.
